1 بَتَكَهُ , aor.
بَتِكَ and
بَتُكَ , (S, K,) inf. n. بَتْكٌ, (S,) He cut it; or severed it, or cut it off, (S, K,) entirely, or from its root; (TA;) and in like manner, ↓ بتّكهُ , (K,) inf. n. تَبْتِيكٌ; (TA;) but بتَك is with teshdeed to denote muchness, or frequency, of the action, or its application to many objects. (S, TA.) آذَانَ الأَنْعَامِ, in the Kur [iv. 118], accord. to Abu-l-'Abbás, (TA,) means And they shall assuredly cut, or cut off, the ears of the cattle: (S, * TA:) or, as Az thinks, slit the ears of the cattle, as they did in the time of ignorance. (TA.) ―
-b2- Also He plucked it out; he laid hold upon it and pulled it towards him so that it became severed from its root and plucked out; (Lth, S, * TA;) namely, a hair, or feather, or the like. (Lth, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
